content.title: What's Cicada? Experts warn of new COVID variant in US; is it in NJ?
content.text: March 26, 2026, 6:41 p.m. ETExperts warn a new pandemic in 2026 could lead to a summer surge in COVID cases as new COVID variant BA 3.2 spreads across the US and 20 other countries.The variant, also called Cicada, had remained hidden "underground" for years, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).While the first COVID-19 case in the US was reported in January 2020, the new COVID-19 variant, Cicada, is a "highly mutated" virus that has steadily been increasing in the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and Kenya, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).Fears of a new summer pandemic 2026 in the US has surged as news of the new virus emerges, with the GISAID database from the CDC reporting cases in 25 states including several in the Northeast, such as New Jersey, Pennsylvania, New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Maryland, Rhode Island and New Hampshire.BA.3.2 Cicada was first detected in the US in June 2025 in a traveler returning from the Netherlands at the San Francisco International Airport, the CDC said. It's now been detected in more international travelers, in wastewater samples, and in COVID patients.Most concerning is the new COVID-19 variant's genetic changes that sets it apart from other COVID-19 variants, Andrew Pekosz, Ph.D., a virologist at John Hopkins told TODAY.According to the CDC, COVID variants Omicron (NB.1.8.1) and Omicron (XFG) are the newest COVID variants circulating in the US. In New Jersey, Omicron XFG accounts for 84% of recently diagnosed cases of COVID, according to the latest New Jersey Department of Health Respiratory Illness Surveillance Report through March 21.What makes the new BA.3.2 Cicada COVID variant different is that it has so many mutations, it may look different to your immune system — which could reduce your protection from a prior COVID vaccine or COVID infection — according to the CDC's latest Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.The "hyper-mutated" variant is now under constant surveillance by the World Health Organization with the CDC watching for a possible summer pandemic in the United States. Here's what to know about the new COVID variant BA.3.2, its potential symptoms and how effective COVID vaccines are against "Cicada."What is the new COVID variant BA 3.2?The new COVID variant BA 3.2, or Cicada, is a "highly mutated" COVID variant, moving slowly and quietly underground, according to the CDC and WHO. It was named Cicada by T. Ryan Gregory, Ph.D, a professor of evolutionary biology at Canada's University of Guelph. Like its namesake insect, BA 3.2 spend its first years under the radar, replicating for years before it spreads.Cicada COVID variant symptomsThe new COVID variant BA 3.2 Cicada symptoms are similar to other COVID variants circulating right now like Omicron and include cough, fever or chills, sore throat, congestion, shortness of breath, loss of smell or taste, fatigue, headache, and gastrointestinal symptoms, per the CDC.Symptoms vary person-to-person and usually go away on their own with, experts say.How effective is a vaccine for COVID Cicada?The new COVID Cicada virus has 70-75 mutations in its "spike protein," scientists say, which makes its "genetically distinct" from other COVID-19 variants, including Alpha, Beta, Gamma, and Delta. Omicron XFG and Omicron NB.1.8.1 (Nimbus) are still very present in the US and across the Northeast, like New Jersey, but this new COVID variant, scientists say, differs, making it likely resistant to the 2025-2026 COVID vaccines. However, more research is needed, the CDC says.COVID vaccines, however, are often reformulated in the summer and can protect against multiple strains.But in the meantime, protect yourself and others by testing if you have symptoms, staying home when sick and wearing a mask in high-risk settings, like crowded, indoor areas. You could also consider getting a COVID-19 booster shot if you are at risk of severe disease from COVID-19, like adults over 65 and those with weakened immune systems.Is the new Cicada virus in NJ? Where is COVID variant CicadaYes, the new COVID variant BA 3.2, or "Cicada," has spread to New Jersey as well as at least 24 other states, per the CDC. Those states where the new COVID-19 variant has been found are:CaliforniaConnecticutFloridaHawaiiIdahoLouisianaMaineMarylandMassachusettsMichiganMissouriNevadaNew HampshireNew JerseyNew YorkOhioPennsylvaniaRhode IslandSouth CarolinaTexasUtahVermontVirginiaWyomingLori Comstock is a New Jersey-based news reporter covering trending news with USA TODAY Network's Mid-Atlantic Connect Team.
